label: copy-phase input j/b early in recall (recall_idx 1-3), rare subset
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.03% of steps). 96% of its activation mass falls in the copy phase, mostly at recall_idx 1-2 (where the input is the fed-back original token 0 or 1). The input token is almost always j (58% of mass) or b (28%). The predicate (copy phase, input j or b, recall_idx <= 3) covers about 81% of activation mass, but precision is only about 1.5%: only around 1 in 70 such steps actually fire. Adding conditions did not recover the missing selectivity. Requiring the next output to be r or 2, an output token in {j,b,r}, r/2 anywhere in the sequence, or a larger L each pushed precision to at most about 10% while recall fell sharply. Top activations come from sequences that start with j/b and are followed by r and 2 (e.g. b r ..., j r 2 ...), and also from a few late original-phase steps in long sequences. The feature never fires at t<4 or on first occurrences of a token, and rarely fires late in the copy phase (recall_idx >= 4). Magnitude is highest for j/b at recall_idx 1 in sequences like b r / j r 2, but I could not find what separates firing from non-firing j/b steps.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=j (+6.29), phase=2 & in_tok=b (+5.30), phase=2 & out_tok=j (+3.98), phase=2 & out_tok=b (+3.43), phase=2 & in_tok=0 (+2.78), in_tok=k (+2.76). Lower it: out_tok=2 (-3.06), prev_tok=r (-2.47), next_out=- (-2.42), orig4=x (-1.89).
